memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then the LORD said to Moses, 'Tell the Israelites this: "You have seen for
yourselves that I have spoken to you from heaven: Do not make any gods to be
alongside me; do not make for yourselves gods of silver or gods of gold. Make an
altar of earth for me and sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and fellowship
offerings, your sheep and goats and your cattle. Wherever I cause my name to be
honored, I will come to you and bless you."'" - Ex 20:22-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After the thunder and the commandments, God gives instructions for worship, and
they are strikingly plain.

An altar of earth. Not gold, not silver, not something impressive. Dirt.

The contrast with Egypt could hardly be sharper. Egypt built enormous temples
covered in precious metal. God asks for soil.

Why? Partly because gold and silver had just been named as materials for idols,
and partly because God is not impressed by expense. What He wants is genuine
sacrifice offered by people who belong to Him.

Notice the promise attached: "Wherever I cause my name to be honored, I will come
to you and bless you." God comes to simple altars.

This should encourage anyone who feels their worship is unimpressive. The prayer
whispered in a crowded house. The small congregation in a rented room. The
believer with no musical ability singing anyway. God has never required a
building to come near.

Jesus told the Samaritan woman that the hour had come when worshippers would
worship "in the Spirit and in truth," not tied to a particular mountain (John
4:23-24).

He comes where His name is honoured. That can be anywhere.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you undervalue your worship because it seems unimpressive?
2. Where has God met you in an ordinary place?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You come to simple altars. Meet me here, in my ordinary
life. Amen.
